rationale_summary: The overview predominantly frames Japan's 2025 AI Act through innovation_enablement, emphasizing proportional governance that promotes R&D and utilization while mitigating risks and explicitly aiming to make Japan 'the friendliest country to develop and utilize AI.' Economic competitiveness is a close runner-up—citing that Japan is 'lagging behind in AI development and use,' 'developing the national economy,' and 'enhancing international competitiveness'—but innovation_enablement edges it out because the act's title, core necessity, basic plan, and concluding model-law vision center on building an enabling R&D and adoption ecosystem rather than pure commercial rivalry. National security and fundamental rights appear as targeted secondary rationales in the basic principles and investigatory measures, while citizen concern and improving people's lives provide a minor public-welfare backdrop.

evidence_spans.quote: Along with existing laws and business acts, a new law is needed to promote innovation while mitigating risks.
